sections.body:
Enter and edit text: a native `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>` with a floating label, optional
adornments and helper text.
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
div[data-ok-text-field][data-ok-variant][data-ok-size][data-ok-margin][data-ok-error]?[data-ok-full-width]?[data-ok-shrink]?[data-ok-min-rows]?[data-ok-max-rows]?
  label[data-ok-text-field-label][for=<input id>]? (› span[data-ok-text-field-asterisk][aria-hidden] " *")
  div[data-ok-text-field-control]
    span[data-ok-text-field-adornment="start"]?
    input[data-ok-text-field-input][id][placeholder]   | textarea[…][rows][placeholder] | select[…] › option
    svg[data-ok-text-field-select-icon][aria-hidden]?  (select)
    span[data-ok-text-field-adornment="end"]?
    fieldset[data-ok-text-field-outline][aria-hidden] › legend? › span (label + " *")   (outlined only)
  div[data-ok-text-field-helper][id]?                  (linked by aria-describedby)
```
Inputs and textareas always carry a `placeholder` (" " when none): `:not(:placeholder-shown)` is
how CSS knows there is a value. React renders `data-ok-runtime="off"` on the root; `ref` and the
remaining props go to the input; `className` / `style` to the root.
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `text-field`: listed under "options".)

React: `label`, `helperText`, `startAdornment` / `endAdornment` (`InputAdornment position`),
`multiline` + `rows`, `select` + `<option>` children, `value` / `defaultValue` /
`onChange(value)`, `id` (default `useId()`), native input props. Renamed: `slotProps.input.*Adornment`
→ `startAdornment` / `endAdornment`, `slotProps.inputLabel.shrink` → `shrink` (no slotProps).
`color` keeps MUI's name and values plus `default` (the text color, as on the reference), which is
the default (MUI: `primary`): lines use the palette's `main`, the focused label its AA `-text` tone.
Listbox `select`: `selectProps={{ native: false, … }}` (MUI `SelectProps` / `slotProps.select`)
with `MenuItem` children composes the Select (select.md) in the control: the control gets
`data-ok-select` (+ `data-ok-auto-width` / `data-ok-display-empty`), the trigger
`div[data-ok-text-field-input][data-ok-select-display][role=combobox]` replaces the `<select>`,
followed by the hidden `input[data-ok-select-input]`, the icon (`data-ok-text-field-select-icon
data-ok-select-icon`), the outline and the Select's popover; the label gets `id` (`<id>-label`).
`select` alone stays native (MUI's default is the listbox; additive, no DOM change). Single
values only (`value` stays a string): use FormControl + Select for `multiple`. Not applicable:
`sx`, `classes`, `slots`, `slotProps`.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
- Text `--ok-font-size-lg` (15px) / 24px; label rest `--ok-text-secondary` 15px (filled:
  `grey-700` in light schemes, AA on the tint), floated 16px × 0.75 semibold; focus
  `--ok-text-primary` (or `--ok-c-text` with `color`); error `--ok-palette-error-text`; disabled
  `--ok-text-disabled`. Transitions `--ok-duration-shorter` `--ok-easing-decelerate`.
- Outlined: border 1px grey-500 at 0.2 → hover text-primary → focus 2px; radius `--ok-radius-md`;
  input padding 16 / 14px (small 8 / 14px) → 56 / 40px; label 14px in, rest y 16 (small 8), up −9.
- Filled: grey-500 tint 0.08 (hover / focus 0.16, disabled 0.24, error error channel 0.08);
  padding 24 12 8 (small 20 12 4; no label 16 12 / 8 12); label x 12, up 6 (small 4); focus adds
  a 2px inset ring (the reference has none).
- Standard: underline 1px grey-500 at 0.32 → hover 2px → focus 2px line growing from the
  middle; label space 16px above; padding 4px 0 (small 2px 0).
- Adornments: `--ok-text-secondary`, 14px semibold, 8px from the input. Helper: caption 12 / 18px,
  margin 6px 12px 0, `--ok-text-secondary` (also when disabled, for AA).
- Select: native, `appearance: none`, own arrow 20px at 7px from the end.
- Multiline: textarea `resize: none`; with min / max rows it grows (`field-sizing: content`,
  `min-height` / `max-height` = rows × 1lh); fallback: `rows` = minRows, scrolls.
sections.title: Layout and tokens

sections.body:
Inline-flex column; `fullWidth` stretches. No breakpoint rules; the label truncates with an
ellipsis, helper text wraps.
sections.title: Responsive behavior

sections.body: `:focus-within`, input `:disabled`, `:placeholder-shown`, `[data-ok-error]`, hover.
sections.title: States

sections.body:
CSS only. HTML runtime `text-field`: `data-ok-min-rows` / `data-ok-max-rows` → `--_ok-min-rows` /
`--_ok-max-rows` (CSSOM, observed); `data-ok-error` → the input's `aria-invalid="true"` (removed
again only if the runtime set it); a `button[data-ok-text-field-reveal]` inside the field toggles
the input between `password` and `text` and sets `aria-pressed` (React apps keep `type` in state).
sections.title: Behavior

sections.body: Native input, textarea and select behavior.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
`<label for>` names the input (no label → `aria-label`); helper via `aria-describedby`; error
sets `aria-invalid`; the asterisk is `aria-hidden` (the input is `required`). The resting label is
`text-secondary`, not the reference's `text-disabled` (AA).
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body: HTML: native `input` / `change`. React: `onChange(value)`.
sections.title: Events / API

sections.body:
React stories render the password button without state (apps own `type`, see the docs page);
`data-ok-text-field-reveal` is an HTML hook (ignored by parity).

components.name: timeline

options.description: Side of the content: `right`, `left`, or alternating from item to item.
options.name: position

options.description: Overrides the timeline's side for this item.
options.name: position

options.description: A filled dot, or a ring.
options.name: variant

options.description: `grey` (default), `inherit` (text color) or a palette color.
options.name: color

sections.body: Events in order along a vertical line. CSS only (no runtime).
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
ul[data-ok-timeline][data-ok-position]
  li[data-ok-timeline-item][data-ok-position]?
    div[data-ok-timeline-opposite-content]?
    div[data-ok-timeline-separator]
      span[data-ok-timeline-dot][data-ok-variant][data-ok-color] › svg[aria-hidden]?
      span[data-ok-timeline-connector]?            (not on the last item)
    div[data-ok-timeline-content]
```
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `timeline`: listed under "options".)

(Options of `timeline-item`: listed under "options".)

(Options of `timeline-dot`: listed under "options".)

API mapping (MUI Lab): kept Timeline `position`; TimelineItem `position`; TimelineDot `variant`,
`color` (`grey` default, `inherit`, primary, secondary + Owlky's info / success / warning /
error, as on the reference); TimelineSeparator, TimelineConnector, TimelineContent,
TimelineOppositeContent. Not applicable: `classes`, `sx`, `component`.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
Root padding 6px 16px, list reset. Item: flex row (left: row-reverse), min-height 70px; without
opposite content a `::before` takes the other half (MUI). Content / opposite: `flex: 1`, padding
6px 16px, body1, `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; content aligned away from the line, opposite toward it.
Dot: 4px padding + 2px border (12px), margin 11.5px 0, `--ok-palette-grey-400` (grey), palette
`main`, `--ok-text-primary` (inherit); outlined: border in the color, transparent fill; an icon is
24px (36px dot). Connector: 2px, `--ok-divider`, grows. Alternate: even items reversed
(`alternate-reverse`: odd).
sections.title: Layout and tokens

sections.body: None (static).
sections.title: States

sections.body:
A list: screen readers announce count and position. Dots are decorative; content carries the
meaning. Text `--ok-text-primary` (AA).
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body: Same at every breakpoint; long words wrap inside their half.
sections.title: Responsive

sections.body: None (no runtime; same markup).

sections.body:
A button that stays pressed (format text, choose a view). Standalone, or in a group with
exclusive (one) or multiple selection.
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
div[role="group"][data-ok-toggle-group][data-ok-orientation][data-ok-exclusive]?[aria-label]
  button[type="button"][data-ok-toggle-button][data-ok-color][data-ok-size][value][aria-pressed]…
    svg[aria-hidden="true"] | text

button[type="button"][data-ok-toggle-button]…[aria-pressed]      (standalone)
```
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `toggle-button`: listed under "options".)

(Options of `toggle-group`: listed under "options".)

Other props (not options):

| HTML | React | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `value` | string identifying the button in a group |
| group value | `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | exclusive: `string \| null`; multiple: `string[]` |

React passes the group's `color`, `size` and `disabled` to every child (a child prop wins).
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
- Unpressed: secondary text color. Pressed: bg `channel` 8 % and `main` text (standard:
  `--ok-action-selected`, primary text); standalone pressed buttons also get a `currentColor` border.
- Standalone: 1px border (grey 20 %). Group: 1px border (grey 16 %), 4px padding and gap; buttons inside
  have no border.
- `:hover` (`hover: hover`): `--ok-action-hover` (colored: `channel` 8 %). `:disabled`:
  `--ok-action-disabled` text; pressed + disabled: `--ok-action-disabled-bg` fill.
sections.title: States

sections.body:
Runtime needed in HTML (React keeps state). Selection logic is shared in core
(`nextToggleSelection()`): exclusive → pressing the pressed button clears the selection, any other
replaces it; multiple → adds or removes the value. Disabled buttons never change.
sections.title: Behavior

sections.body: Native buttons: `Tab` to each button, `Enter` / `Space` toggle.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
`aria-pressed` carries the state; the group is `role="group"` (add `aria-label`). Icon-only buttons
need `aria-label`.
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body:
HTML, cancelable (call `preventDefault()` to keep the current state):
- `ok:toggle-button:change` on a standalone button — `detail: { pressed }` (the new state).
- `ok:toggle-group:change` on the group — `detail: { value, previous, button }` (`value` shaped as
  in the options table).

Instances: `runtime.get(el, "toggle-button")` → `{ pressed, setPressed(pressed) }`;
`runtime.get(el, "toggle-group")` → `{ value, setValue(value) }` (setters don't emit events).
React: `onChange(selected)` on a standalone `ToggleButton`, `onChange(value)` on `ToggleButtonGroup`;
both work controlled and uncontrolled.
sections.title: Events / API

sections.body: Same size at every breakpoint; use `vertical` for narrow screens.
sections.title: Responsive

sections.body: React renders `data-ok-runtime="off"` on the group and on standalone buttons.
sections.title: Parity notes

sections.body:
A short text label on hover, focus or long press. Runtime behavior: core `createHoverIntent`
(timing) + `createPopoverController` (positioning; no focus move, no outside dismiss).
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
trigger[aria-labelledby="id"] | trigger[aria-describedby="id"]      (describeChild)
div[data-ok-tooltip][role=tooltip][popover=manual][id][data-ok-placement][data-ok-arrow]?[data-ok-transition]?
  › span[data-ok-tooltip-arrow][aria-hidden]       (always rendered; shown with data-ok-arrow)
  › text
```
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `tooltip`: listed under "options".)

React: `title`, one element `children` (cloned: relation attribute, pointer / focus handlers,
merged ref), `describeChild`, `open` / `onOpenChange(open)`, `enterTouchDelay` (700),
`leaveTouchDelay` (1500), `disableHoverListener`, `disableFocusListener`,
`disableTouchListener`. Renamed: `TransitionComponent` (Grow / Fade / Zoom) → `transition`;
`onOpen` / `onClose` → `onOpenChange`. Kept behavior: `describeChild=false` names the trigger
(MUI sets `aria-label`; we use `aria-labelledby`, same name). Deferred: `followCursor`,
`enterNextDelay`, `disableInteractive` (always hoverable, WCAG 1.4.13). Not applicable:
`PopperProps`, `slots`, `slotProps`, `components`, `sx`.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
`--ok-palette-grey-800` (dark scheme grey-700, via `light-dark()`), white text, 11px (font-size-xs −
1px) 500 / 1.5, padding 4px 8px, radius `--ok-radius-sm`, max width 300px. Gap 8px (10px with the
arrow); arrow 10px. Transitions: grow (scale 0.75) / fade / zoom, `--ok-duration-shortest`.
`--ok-z-tooltip` in the fallback.

sections.body: Flips and shifts to stay 16px inside the viewport.

Keyboard / Accessibility

sections.body:
HTML: `ok:tooltip:open` (`detail.trigger`), `ok:tooltip:close`. Instance: `{ isOpen, show(trigger?),
hide() }`. Triggers are found by delegation (`aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` pointing at a
`[data-ok-tooltip]`).

Move items between two lists. A composite of existing components (Scrollbar, List, Checkbox,
Button) with its layout in `transfer-list.css`; the rules are core `transferMove` / `canTransfer`
/ `toggleAll` / `sideCheckedState`. HTML runtime `transfer-list` moves the rows.
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
div[data-ok-transfer-list][data-ok-variant][data-ok-disabled]?[data-ok-label-count]?
  section[data-ok-transfer-list-panel][data-ok-side="left"]
    div[data-ok-transfer-list-header]?                       (enhanced)
      span[data-ok-checkbox] (select all, aria-label) · span[data-ok-transfer-list-title] · span[data-ok-transfer-list-count]
    section[data-ok-scrollbar][aria-label="Choices"][tabindex=0]
      ul[data-ok-list][data-ok-disable-padding]
        li[data-ok-list-item][data-ok-disable-padding][data-ok-value]
          label[data-ok-transfer-list-option] › span[data-ok-checkbox] (input[id]) + span (label)
  div[data-ok-transfer-list-actions]
    button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant=outlined][data-ok-size=sm][data-ok-transfer-list-move][aria-label] › svg
  section[data-ok-transfer-list-panel][data-ok-side="right"] …
```
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `transfer-list`: listed under "options".)

Other props: `items` (`{ value, label }[]`), `left` / `right` (controlled) or `defaultLeft`,
`onChange(left, right)`, `titles` (`["Choices", "Chosen"]`), `getCountLabel(checked, total)`
(HTML `data-ok-label-count="{checked}/{total} selected"`), `buttonLabels`, `id` (prefix of the
checkbox ids).
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
Panels 220px (`spacing` × 55, max 100%), `--ok-bg-paper`, `--ok-shadow-card`, `--ok-radius-xl`;
list area 200px tall (scrolls in its Scrollbar), list padding 8px 0. Rows: min 44px, padding 4px
8px, gap 4px, subtitle2 type, hover `--ok-action-hover`; the 40px checkbox gets −2px block margins.
Header: grid (checkbox spanning title + caption count), 8px padding, `--ok-divider` bottom line.
Buttons: outlined `sm`, 16px arrows. Mobile first: panels stacked, buttons in a row with arrows
turned 90°; from 600px panels side by side (gap 24px), buttons in a column.
sections.title: Layout and tokens

sections.body:
Check rows; move buttons (`all-right` · `right` · `left` · `all-left`; enhanced: `right` / `left`)
move the checked (or all) rows to the end of the other list and uncheck them. Buttons that would
move nothing are disabled. Enhanced: select-all checks / clears a side, shows mixed
(`indeterminate` + `data-ok-indeterminate`), counts follow.

sections.body: Native: Tab through the scroll areas, checkboxes and buttons; Space toggles / presses.

```
      span[data-ok-tree-item-icon] › svg[data-ok-tree-chevron] | span[data-ok-tree-expand-icon] + span[data-ok-tree-collapse-icon] | end icon
      span[data-ok-tree-item-checkbox][aria-hidden]? › span[data-ok-checkbox] (small, tabindex -1)
      span[data-ok-tree-item-label]
    ul[data-ok-collapse][role=group][data-ok-tree-item-group][hidden]?      (branches only; a Collapse)
```
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `tree-view`: listed under "options".)

Other props: `expandedItems` / `defaultExpandedItems` / `onExpandedItemsChange(ids)`,
`onItemExpansionToggle(id, expanded)`, `selectedItems` / `defaultSelectedItems` /
`onSelectedItemsChange` (`string | null`, `string[]` when multi), `expandIcon`, `collapseIcon`,
`endIcon`; TreeItem `itemId`, `label`, `disabled`; RichTreeView `items` (`{ id, label,
children?, disabled? }[]`).

API mapping (MUI X): kept the props above, `multiSelect`, `checkboxSelection` (implies multi),
`disableSelection`, `expansionTrigger`. Renamed: `slots.expandIcon` / `collapseIcon` / `endIcon`
→ props. Beyond MUI X (reference "Custom styling"): `variant="lines"`. Deferred:
`selectionPropagation`, drag and drop (`itemsReordering`), lazy loading, `apiRef`,
`getItemId` / `getItemLabel`, label editing. Not applicable: `slots`, `slotProps`, `sx`.
Group transition (MUI X `slots.groupTransition`, default Collapse): each group is a Collapse
(collapse.md, ADR-0044; React `TreeItem` renders `Collapse component="ul"`, HTML snippets carry
`data-ok-collapse`); the runtime still writes the group's `hidden`, the Collapse animates it.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
Rows: min 30px, padding 4px 8px (+12px per level, up to 6 levels, rows stay full width), gap 8px,
`--ok-radius-md`; icon 18px; label body2. Hover `--ok-action-hover`; selected
`rgb(primary / 0.08)` (checkbox selection: the checkbox shows it); focus-visible 2px outline +
`--ok-action-focus`; disabled 0.48. Chevron turns 90° when open (`--ok-duration-shortest`).
Lines: groups indented 17px with a 1px dashed `rgb(grey-500 / 0.4)` guide, rows `--ok-radius-xs`,
labels 13px medium, expand icons round `rgb(primary / 0.25)`, selected `rgb(primary / 0.2)`.

sections.body:
Click on the row (or only the icon with `iconContainer`) toggles a branch; click selects (multi:

options.description: A step of the type scale (font, size, weight, line height, case); `inherit` keeps the parent's font.

sections.body:
Text in one step of the type scale (`--ok-typography-<variant>-*` tokens of `@owlky/tokens`,
responsive at the token breakpoints). CSS only; the element is the author's choice.
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
<element>[data-ok-typography][data-ok-variant][data-ok-color]?[data-ok-align]?[data-ok-gutter-bottom]?[data-ok-no-wrap]?
```
React picks the element from `variantMapping` (default below) unless `component` is given;
HTML authors write it.

| Variant | `h1`–`h6` | `subtitle1`, `subtitle2` | `body1`, `body2`, `inherit` | `caption`, `overline`, `button` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Element | `h1`–`h6` | `h6` | `p` | `span` |
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `typography`: listed under "options".)

React: `children`, `component` (any element type), `variantMapping` (partial, merged over the
default), `ref` (the rendered element), every attribute of the element (`htmlFor`, `id`…).
Not applicable: `sx`, `classes`, `paragraph` (deprecated upstream: `component="p"` +
`gutterBottom`), theme-level `variantMapping` / custom variants (consumer CSS on
`[data-ok-variant="…"]` or the tokens), arbitrary color strings such as `"text.secondary"` /
`"primary.dark"` (use `style` / CSS).
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
`margin: 0`. Each variant: `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `line-height`,
`text-transform` from `--ok-typography-<variant>-*` (h1–h3 use the secondary font family through
the tokens; font presets apply). `inherit`: `font: inherit; text-transform: inherit`. Colors:
palette `--ok-c-main` (the `[data-ok-color]` binding), `--ok-text-primary|secondary|disabled`.
`gutterBottom`: `margin-block-end: 0.35em`. `noWrap`: `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
white-space: nowrap`. `typography.css` loads first in `owlky.css` so components that compose
Typography restyle it through their own CSS (same zero specificity, later wins).

Unknown values (HTML) get no rule: the text keeps the parent's font, color and alignment.
sections.title: Layout and tokens

sections.body:
Fluid. Heading sizes (h1–h6) step up at 600 / 900 / 1200px through the tokens; text wraps
except with `noWrap` (one line, ellipsis).
sections.title: Responsive behavior

sections.body:
Not focusable. Variant and element are independent: keep the heading outline (`component`).
Sizes in `rem`. Palette colors use `main` (ADR-0014, exempt from `color-contrast` like other
brand text); `textPrimary` / `textSecondary` meet AA; `textDisabled` is for inactive content.

components.name: upload

options.description: `default`: a drop zone with an illustration; `avatar`: a round photo picker; `box`: a small box.
options.name: variant

options.description: File list: rows with names and sizes, or a wrapping row of tiles.
options.name: layout

options.description: Image files show a preview; `false` shows the file type icon instead.
options.name: thumbnail

options.description: Accepts several files and keeps adding them.
options.name: multiple

options.description: Can't receive files (input disabled, dimmed).
options.name: disabled

options.description: Error colors on the zone and the helper text.
options.name: error

options.description: Most files the upload holds (multiple; 0 = no limit). The others are rejected.
options.name: maxFiles

options.description: Largest accepted file, in bytes.
options.name: maxSize

options.description: Smallest accepted file, in bytes.
options.name: minSize

options.description: A press on the zone doesn't open the file dialog.
options.name: noClick

options.description: The input leaves the tab order (give people another way to open the dialog).
options.name: noKeyboard

options.description: Files can't be dropped on the zone.
options.name: noDrag

options.description: Drags handled here don't reach an outer upload.
options.name: noDragEventsBubbling

options.description: Pasting files while the upload has focus does nothing.
options.name: noPaste

options.description: Files dropped outside an upload don't open in the tab.
options.name: preventDropOnDocument

options.description: Opens the File System Access picker where supported (the input otherwise).
options.name: useFsAccessApi

options.description: The files the upload holds (`value` / `defaultValue`).
options.name: value

sections.body:
Let people choose files by dropping them on a zone, pressing it (file dialog), pressing Enter or
Space, or pasting; check each file (type, size, count, a custom validator); keep the accepted
files (single: replace; multiple: add), show them (preview in the zone, or a list of rows / tiles
with thumbnails, names and sizes) and list the rejected ones with their reasons. No network: the
owner sends the files. The files are mirrored into the native input (`DataTransfer`), so a form
submits them.
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
div[data-ok-upload][data-ok-variant][data-ok-layout] …options
    (+ controller state: data-ok-drag="accept|reject|unknown", data-ok-drag-global, aria-busy)
  div[data-ok-upload-zone]
    input[type=file][data-ok-upload-input][title=" "][aria-labelledby=<title> | aria-label]
         [aria-describedby=<helper>]? [aria-invalid]? [multiple]? [accept]? [disabled]? [tabindex=-1 with noKeyboard]
         (covers the zone, opacity 0: a press opens the dialog, a drop fills it, even without JS)
    div[data-ok-upload-placeholder]
      default: svg[data-ok-illustration="upload"][data-ok-color="primary"][data-ok-upload-illustration][aria-hidden]
               (the illustration set's `upload` picture by composition, specs/components/illustration.md;
               shapes carry data-ok-tone, colors from illustration.css, the 200px width from upload.css)
               div[data-ok-upload-placeholder-text]
                 span[data-ok-upload-title][id]   "Drop or select a file" / "…files"
                 span[data-ok-upload-description] "Drag … or " span[data-ok-upload-browse] " your device."
      avatar:  svg[data-ok-upload-icon] + span[data-ok-upload-title][id][data-ok-label-upload][data-ok-label-update]
      box:     svg[data-ok-upload-icon] (cloud), or the placeholder content
    span[data-ok-upload-preview][id]?          (single file, default and avatar)
      › img[alt=<name>] | span[data-ok-upload-file] + span[data-ok-upload-preview-name] + span[data-ok-upload-preview-size]
    button[data-ok-icon-button][data-ok-size=sm][data-ok-upload-remove][id][aria-labelledby="<self> <preview>"][hidden]?
      › span[data-ok-upload-remove-text] "Remove" + svg      (single file, default variant)
  div[data-ok-upload-helper-text][id]?
  div[data-ok-upload-rejections][role=alert]   (empty until a drop is rejected)
    › ul › li › span[data-ok-upload-rejection-file] "name - size" + span[data-ok-upload-rejection-error] "- message" …
  ul[data-ok-upload-list][aria-live=polite]    (multiple, default variant)
    › li[data-ok-upload-item]
        span[data-ok-upload-thumb] › img[alt=""] | span[data-ok-upload-file][data-ok-kind][aria-hidden] › svg + span[data-ok-upload-file-ext]
        span[data-ok-upload-item-text] › span[data-ok-upload-item-name][id] + span[data-ok-upload-item-size]?
        button[data-ok-icon-button][data-ok-size=sm][data-ok-upload-remove][id][aria-labelledby="<self> <name>"] › span[data-ok-upload-remove-text] + svg
  template[data-ok-upload-template] › li[data-ok-upload-item] …(HTML only: the row the runtime clones)
  div[data-ok-upload-actions][hidden while empty]?   (React: with onRemoveAll / onUpload)
    › button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant=outlined][data-ok-size=sm][data-ok-upload-remove-all]
    › button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant=contained][data-ok-size=sm][data-ok-upload-submit] (cloud start icon)
```
Any `[data-ok-upload-open]` inside the root opens the dialog (both implementations).
`data-ok-kind`: image · video · audio · pdf · document · spreadsheet · presentation · archive ·
text · code · other (from the extension, then the MIME type).
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `upload`: listed under "options".)

Outside the schema:
- `accept` (input attribute; React also `{ [mime]: extensions[] }` and labeled groups
  `{ description, accept }[]`, which label the File System Access picker's rows). Only valid MIME
  types, `type/*` and `.ext` survive; a wildcard paired with extensions keeps the extensions.
- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(files)`: `(File | string)[]`; strings are URLs of files
  chosen before (shown by name, not put in the input). HTML: `files`, `setFiles()`,
  `ok:upload:change` (`{ files, reason: "add" | "remove" | "clear" | "reset" }`).
- `helperText`, `title`, `description`, `placeholder` (ReactNode or `(state) => ReactNode`),
  `labels` (`remove`, `removeAll`, `upload`, `uploadPhoto`, `updatePhoto`), `locale` (sizes).
- `validator(file)` (sync or async; HTML `setValidator`), `getErrorMessage(error, file)` (HTML
  `setErrorMessage`), `getFilesFromEvent(event | handles)` (HTML `setFilesFromEvent`).
- Callbacks: `onDrop(accepted, rejections)`, `onDropAccepted`, `onDropRejected`,
  `onFileDialogOpen`, `onFileDialogCancel`, `onError`, `onRemove(file)`, `onRemoveAll()`,
  `onUpload(files)`; native drag events on the root (`onDragEnter` …) pass through.
- Input attributes: `name`, `form`, `required`, `capture`, `inputId`, `inputRef`, `autoFocus`
  (HTML `autofocus`), `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`.
- `apiRef`: `open()`, `removeFile(file)`, `clearFiles()`, `files`, `rejections`.
- Components: `Upload`, `UploadAvatar` (`variant="avatar"`, `accept="image/*"`), `UploadBox`
  (`variant="box"`, `multiple` by default), `UploadCloudIcon`.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
- Drag: `data-ok-drag` while files are over the zone — `accept` (primary border), `reject`
  (error colors: too many files, or a known MIME type outside `accept`), `unknown` (decided at
  drop: extensions, a validator); `data-ok-drag-global` while files are dragged over the page.
- Busy: `aria-busy="true"` while files are read or an async validator runs.
- Error: `data-ok-error` (zone and helper text in error colors, input `aria-invalid`).
- Disabled: the input's `disabled` (zone at 0.48 opacity, no drops, no dialog).
- Focus: the input's `:focus-visible` draws the zone's outline.
- Hover (pointer devices) and drags: a grey 500 border (the reference dims the zone to 0.72,
  which takes the description below AA).
sections.title: States

sections.body:
- Core `createUploadController` (both implementations): drag enter / over / leave / drop on the
  root (target counting, verdict, `dropEffect`), drops always prevented inside the root; folders
  read recursively (`webkitGetAsEntry`); paste of files (`noPaste`); Enter on the input and
  `[data-ok-upload-open]` → `open()`; `noClick` (CSS `pointer-events: none` on the input + JS
  refusal of pointer clicks); `useFsAccessApi` → `showOpenFilePicker` (AbortError → cancel,
  NotAllowed / SecurityError → the input); `cancel` event / empty `change` → dialog cancel (the
  held files go back into the input); form `reset` → cleared; `preventDropOnDocument` (document
  `dragover` / `drop` outside uploads prevented); `noDragEventsBubbling` (inner upload claims
  the event, outer ones skip it; no `stopPropagation`). The latest drop wins over pending async
  checks.
- Checks (core `evaluateUploadFiles`): type, `maxSize`, `minSize`, validator errors per file; then
  `too-many-files` past the limit (single: 1; multiple: `maxFiles` minus the files held).
- Owners: single → a new accepted file replaces the old one; multiple → added. Rejections show the
  latest drop's. Object URLs for image previews are revoked when the file leaves and on unmount /
  destroy. After removing with a focused button, the focus moves to the next remove button, else
  the input.
- HTML runtime `upload`: renders the preview, the list (template clones, kept per file), the
  rejections, the avatar title and the actions' `hidden`; `noKeyboard` → `tabindex=-1`.
sections.title: Behavior

sections.body:
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | The input (zone), then remove and action buttons |
| Enter / Space | Opens the file dialog (not with `noKeyboard`) |
| Ctrl/Cmd + V | Pastes files (not with `noPaste`) |
| Enter / Space on a remove button | Removes the file; focus moves on |
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
The native file input is the control (named by the title or `aria-label`, described by the
helper text). Rejections are an alert; the list is a polite live region. Remove buttons are named
"Remove <file name>". Text: description and helper text in `text-secondary`, "browse" in the
primary AA text tone, error texts in the error AA tone. File names are always text
(`textContent` / React children). A disabled zone is dimmed (inactive component, exempt from
contrast in tests).
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body:
HTML events (on the root): `ok:upload:drop` (cancelable, `{ accepted, rejections }`),
`ok:upload:change` (`{ files, reason }`), `ok:upload:remove` (cancelable, `{ file }`),
`ok:upload:upload` (`{ files }`), `ok:upload:dialogopen`, `ok:upload:dialogcancel`,
`ok:upload:drag` (`{ active, verdict, global }`), `ok:upload:error` (`{ error }`).
Instance: `files`, `rejections`, `dragState`, `isFileDialogActive`, `isProcessing`, `open()`,
`setFiles()`, `removeFile()`, `clearFiles()`, `setValidator()`, `setErrorMessage()`,
`setFilesFromEvent()`.
sections.title: Events / API

sections.body:
The zone, list and actions fill their container at every width; names are cut with an ellipsis;
tiles wrap; the description wraps; actions wrap and stay at the end. No breakpoint changes.
sections.title: Responsive

sections.body:
- The HTML list item comes from `<template data-ok-upload-template>` (skipped by parity).
- Ids differ (React `useId`, HTML from the input's id or `createId`); parity normalizes them.
- Image previews are object URLs (different per page): dynamic parity runs with `thumbnail` off.
sections.title: Parity notes

sections.body:
| Upstream | Owlky | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `accept`, `multiple`, `maxFiles`, `maxSize`, `minSize`, `disabled` | kept | `multiple` defaults to `false` (Minimals' Upload); `maxFiles` counts the files held |
| `noClick`, `noKeyboard`, `noDrag`, `noDragEventsBubbling`, `noPaste`, `preventDropOnDocument`, `useFsAccessApi`, `autoFocus` | kept | `noDragEventsBubbling` without `stopPropagation` (outer uploads skip claimed events) |
| `validator`, `getFilesFromEvent`, `getErrorMessage`, `onError` | kept | |
| `onDrop(accepted, rejections, event)` | `onDrop(accepted, rejections)` | value-first (ADR-0015) |
| `onDropAccepted`, `onDropRejected`, `onFileDialogOpen`, `onFileDialogCancel` | kept | cancel from the native `cancel` event |
| `onDragEnter` / `onDragOver` / `onDragLeave` | native root props | state via `placeholder(state)` / `data-ok-drag` |
| `isDragActive` / `Accept` / `Reject` / `Unknown` / `Global`, `isFileDialogActive`, `isProcessing` | `UploadState` | `isFocused` → CSS `:focus-visible` |
| `open`, `removeFile`, `clearFiles`, `acceptedFiles`, `fileRejections` | `apiRef` (`files`, `rejections`) | |
| `getRootProps` / `getInputProps` / `rootRef` / `inputRef` | the component; `inputRef` | hook form deferred (backlog) |
| Minimals: `value`, `error`, `helperText`, `thumbnail`, `onRemove`, `onRemoveAll`, `onUpload`, `placeholder`, `disabled` | kept | "Horizontal layout" → `layout` |

sections.body:
Guide people through a page one step at a time. Each step is a dialog next to the element it
explains, over an overlay that dims the page and leaves a rounded spotlight on that element; or a
pulsing beacon on the element that opens the step. One core controller renders the state the
owner keeps (React state, the HTML runtime) and reports intent (ADR-0004).
sections.title: Purpose

sections.body:
```
div[data-ok-walktour][data-ok-run]? …options                    (controller: data-ok-status="running")
  div[data-ok-backdrop][data-ok-invisible][data-ok-walktour-overlay][popover="manual"][aria-hidden="true"]
      (controller: data-ok-open, data-ok-spotlight-clicks, data-ok-fallback)
    svg[data-ok-walktour-spotlight][aria-hidden="true"][focusable="false"]
      path[data-ok-walktour-mask][fill-rule="evenodd"]   (d: the viewport minus the cut-out)
      path[data-ok-walktour-hole]                        (d: the cut-out; blocks presses unless spotlight clicks)
  button[type="button"][data-ok-walktour-beacon][aria-label="Open the dialog"][aria-haspopup="dialog"][hidden]
    span[data-ok-walktour-beacon-inner]                  (CSSOM: --_ok-walktour-beacon-x / -y)
  div[popover="manual"][data-ok-popover][data-ok-arrow][data-ok-walktour-step][role="dialog"]
     [data-ok-target="<selector>"]?[data-ok-placement]…step options and overrides
     [aria-labelledby="<title id>" | aria-label="Step 1 of 5"][aria-describedby="<content id>"]
     (controller: data-ok-open, data-ok-current-placement, data-ok-centered, aria-modal="true";
      CSSOM --_ok-popover-x / -y / -arrow, --_ok-walktour-width)            one per step
    span[data-ok-popover-arrow][aria-hidden="true"]
    div[data-ok-walktour-header]
      h2[data-ok-walktour-title][id]?
      button[data-ok-icon-button][data-ok-size="sm"][data-ok-walktour-action="close"][aria-label="Close"] › svg
    div[data-ok-walktour-content][id]
    span[role="progressbar"][data-ok-linear-progress][data-ok-variant="determinate"][aria-valuenow][aria-hidden="true"]
    div[data-ok-walktour-footer]
      button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant="text"][data-ok-walktour-action="skip"]        Skip
      button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant="outlined"][data-ok-walktour-action="back"]    Back
      button[data-ok-button][data-ok-variant="contained"][data-ok-color="inherit|primary"][data-ok-walktour-action="primary"]
        Next | Close | Last, span[data-ok-walktour-progress] " (1/5)" (not on the last step)
  span[data-ok-walktour-live][aria-live="polite"][aria-atomic="true"][data-ok-format="Step {current} of {total}"]
```
Composes Backdrop (overlay), Popover (step paper, arrow, positioning, top layer), IconButton,
Button and LinearProgress. Buttons the options turn off get `hidden` from the controller in both
implementations (`[hidden]` rule in walktour.css: Buttons have an author `display`).
sections.title: Anatomy

sections.body:
(Options of `walktour`: listed under "options".)

Step options (React step fields; HTML attributes on the step element):
(Options of `walktour-step`: listed under "options".)

- **Step overrides:** every boolean option of the tour except `scrollToFirstStep` can be set on a
  step (`disableBeacon: true`, `showSkipButton: false`). HTML: the same attribute on the step;
  present = on, `"false"` = off, absent = the tour's.
- **target:** React `string` (CSS selector) · element · ref · `() => element`; HTML
  `data-ok-target="<selector>"`. `"body"` or `placement="center"` centers the step. A target that
  isn't in the page skips the step (`error:target-not-found`). Invalid selectors are no target.
- **content / title:** React nodes; HTML: the step's markup. **stepProps** (React): extra
  attributes of the step element (`data-ok-theme="dark"`).
- **locale:** `back`, `close`, `last`, `next`, `open` (beacon), `skip`, `progress`
  (`"({current}/{total})"`), `stepOf` (`"Step {current} of {total}"`: live region, name of a step
  without a title); per tour and per step. HTML: the text in the markup, `data-ok-format` on the
  live region.
- **run** (default `false`), **stepIndex** (controlled), **initialStepIndex** (HTML
  `data-ok-step-index`), **apiRef**.
sections.title: Options

sections.body:
`idle` → `running` (lifecycle `beacon` | `tooltip`) → `paused` | `finished` | `skipped`.
Core `walktourTransition` (react-joyride's rules):
- `start`: the first available step from the given / current index (an ended tour starts over),
  with its beacon unless `disableBeacon`.
- `next` (primary in a continuous tour): next step's tooltip; `close` (X, Escape, overlay, primary
  in a non-continuous tour): next step's beacon (tooltip with `disableBeacon`); past the last
  step: `finished`. `prev`: previous step (tooltip when continuous). `go(index)`.
- `skip` → `skipped`; `stop` → `paused`; `open` (beacon) → tooltip; `reset` → `idle`, index 0.
- Steps whose target is missing are passed over in the direction of travel.
sections.title: States

sections.body:
- Tooltip: the step opens as a Popover anchored to its target, `offset` = spotlight padding +
  20px (arrow), flipping and shifting to stay in the viewport; `auto` = the side with the most
  room; centered steps are placed by CSS (`data-ok-centered`, no arrow, no cut-out).
- Overlay: shown under the step in the top layer (fallback: fixed + z-index) unless
  `disableOverlay`; the mask path is `M0 0HwVhH0Z` + a rounded rectangle (spotlight padding and
  radius) drawn `evenodd`; recomputed on scroll, resize and target resize (rAF).
- Scrolling: a target (with its tooltip) out of view scrolls into view in its scroll parent,
  `scrollOffset` px from the top (not for the first step without `scrollToFirstStep`; never with
  `disableScrolling`); instant with reduced motion.
- Beacon: a 36px button centered on the edge the placement faces (alignment = the placement's).
- Decorations per step: Back hidden on the first step or with `hideBackButton`; Skip shown with
  `showSkipButton` except on the last step; close hidden with `hideCloseButton`; progress shown
  with `showProgress` except on the last step; `--_ok-walktour-width` from `width`.
- HTML: `data-ok-run` starts / pauses (observed); other option attributes re-render at once.
sections.title: Behavior

sections.body:
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the step's controls; wraps inside a modal step |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button or the beacon |
| Escape | `close` (unless `disableCloseOnEsc`) |
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- Each step is `role="dialog"` named by its title (or "Step 1 of 5") and described by its content;
  `aria-modal="true"` while the overlay blocks the page (not with `spotlightClicks` or
  `disableOverlay`), then Tab stays inside and the page outside the tour is `inert` (core
  `inertOutside`; `aria-hidden` where `inert` is unsupported) until the step closes.
- Focus: the primary button when a step opens (else the first control); the beacon when a step
  closes to it; back to where it was when the tour ends. Starting with a beacon doesn't move focus.
- A polite live region announces "Step 2 of 5" when a step opens. The progress bar is
  `aria-hidden` (the live region and the button say the same).
- The beacon's pulse stops with reduced motion; buttons are ≥ 24px.
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body:
- React: `onStepChange(index, { action, origin, status, lifecycle })` (controlled: the request),
  `onStatusChange(status, { action, index })`, `onEvent(type, data)` with `type` in
  `tour:start`, `step:before`, `beacon`, `tooltip`, `step:after`, `tour:end`, `tour:status`,
  `error:target-not-found` and `data` = `{ type, action, origin, index, status, lifecycle, size }`
  (react-joyride's `callback`, value first).
- HTML: `ok:walktour:beforechange` (cancelable; `{ index, previousIndex, action, origin }`),
  `ok:walktour:change` (the state + `previousIndex`), `ok:walktour:event` (the same data as
  `onEvent`). Trigger `[data-ok-walktour-start="<id>"]` (+ `data-ok-index`) starts the tour over.
- API (`apiRef` / `runtime.get(root, "walktour")`): `state`, `start(index?)`, `stop()`,
  `reset(restart?)`, `next()`, `prev()`, `go(index)`, `close()`, `skip()`, `open()`.
sections.title: Events / API

sections.body:
| Upstream | Owlky |
|---|---|
| `steps`, `run`, `stepIndex`, `continuous`, `showProgress`, `scrollToFirstStep`, `scrollOffset`, `spotlightPadding`, `spotlightRadius` (v3), `locale`, step `target` / `content` / `title` / `placement` (incl. `auto`, `center`) | kept |
| `showSkipButton`, `hideBackButton`, `hideCloseButton`, `disableBeacon`, `disableCloseOnEsc`, `disableOverlay`, `disableOverlayClose`, `disableScrolling`, `spotlightClicks` (v2) | kept (v3: `buttons`, `skipBeacon`, `dismissKeyAction`, `hideOverlay`, `overlayClickAction`, `skipScroll`, `blockTargetInteraction`) |
| `initialStepIndex` (v3), step `width` (v3) | kept |
| `callback` / `onEvent` | `onEvent(type, data)` + `onStepChange`, `onStatusChange` (ADR-0015) |
| `getHelpers` / `useJoyride().controls` | `apiRef` |
| `locale.nextWithProgress` | `next` + `progress` (`"({current}/{total})"`, the reference's look) |
| `styles`, `floatingOptions`, `*Component` (tooltip, beacon, arrow, loader), `portalElement`, `nonce`, `debug`, `zIndex`, colors, arrow sizes | not applicable (CSS tokens, top layer, `data-ok-theme`; markup is the component in HTML) |
| `before` / `after` hooks, `targetWaitTimeout`, `beaconTrigger: "hover"`, `closeButtonAction`, `scrollTarget`, `spotlightTarget`, `isFixed`, `disableFocusTrap`, `beaconPlacement`, `scrollDuration` | deferred (roadmap backlog) |
sections.title: API mapping (react-joyride)

sections.body:
- The controller writes the derived state in both (open step, overlay, `hidden`, `aria-modal`,
  positions, the cut-out, the live text): no parity exception. `data-ok-walktour-start` is an
  HTML trigger (React: `apiRef` from a click handler), ignored by parity.

sections.body: An accordion shows a list of sections that people can expand and collapse in place, such as a FAQ or groups of settings. It keeps long pages short while every answer stays on the page. Accordions are native `<details>` elements, so they open, close and work with find-in-page even without JavaScript.
sections.html:
How do I reset my password?
Open Settings, choose Security and select Reset password.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Three variants are available. `default` turns the open item into a raised card, `outlined` draws one bordered list, and `soft` shows each item as a filled block. Set `disableGutters` to remove the space around the open item.
sections.html:
How do I reset my password?
Open Settings, choose Security and select Reset password.
sections.react:
<Accordion variant="outlined">
  <AccordionSummary>How do I reset my password?</AccordionSummary>
  <AccordionDetails>Open Settings, choose Security and select Reset password.</AccordionDetails>
</Accordion>
sections.title: Choose a variant

sections.body: Give every item in the group the same `name`. Opening one item then closes the others, as the browser does for `<details name>`. Where a browser doesn't support it yet, Owlky closes the others itself.
sections.html:
How do I reset my password?
Open Settings, choose Security and select Reset password.
Can I change my plan later?
Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade at any time from Billing.
Where can I download invoices?
Every invoice is listed in Billing, under History.
sections.title: Open one item at a time

sections.body: In React, pass `expanded` and `onChange` to decide when an item opens, or `defaultExpanded` to only set the initial state. To refuse a change, don't update `expanded`. In HTML, listen to `ok:accordion:beforetoggle` and call `preventDefault()`.
sections.html:
<script type="module">
  document.addEventListener("ok:accordion:beforetoggle", (event) => {
    if (event.detail.open && !userIsSignedIn) event.preventDefault();
  });
</script>
sections.title: Control the open state

sections.body: Every option works the same way in both versions: a prop in React, an attribute in HTML. Values that aren't listed fall back to the default.
sections.title: Options

sections.body: These props and parts set the content. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body:
- **`ok:accordion:beforetoggle`** (cancelable) fires when a summary is activated, with `detail.open`, the requested state.
- **`ok:accordion:toggle`** fires after the item opened or closed, with `detail.open`.
- **Instance:** `runtime.get(element, "accordion")` returns `{ isOpen, toggle(open?) }`.
- **React:** `onChange(expanded)`. A controlled accordion refuses a change by keeping `expanded`.
sections.title: Events and methods

sections.body: The summary is a native disclosure button, so the browser provides the keyboard behavior.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- The summary works as a disclosure button: assistive technology announces whether the item is expanded.
- Put a heading inside each summary, such as an `<h3>`, so the sections appear in the page outline.
- A disabled item is marked `aria-disabled="true"` and removed from the tab order.
- Content stays in the page when closed, so find-in-page can open the item that contains a match.
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body: An alert shows a short, important message, such as the result of an action or a problem that needs attention. Its severity sets the icon and the color: `success`, `info`, `warning` or `error`. Keep the message brief, and add an action when people can fix the problem right away.
sections.html: A new version is available.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Three variants are available: `standard` (the default) is a soft tinted panel, `filled` uses the full color for urgent messages, and `outlined` adds a border. Set `color` to use a different color than the severity's.
sections.html: A new version is available.
sections.react: <Alert severity="info" variant="filled">A new version is available.</Alert>
sections.title: Choose a variant

sections.body: A title sums up the message when it needs more than one sentence. In React, use `AlertTitle`; in HTML, add a `data-ok-alert-title` element at the start of the message.
sections.html:
Update available
Version 2.4 adds offline mode. Restart the app to install it.
sections.react:
<Alert severity="info">
  <AlertTitle>Update available</AlertTitle>
  Version 2.4 adds offline mode. Restart the app to install it.
</Alert>
sections.title: Add a title

sections.body: In React, pass buttons with `action`, or pass `onClose` to show a close button and remove the alert yourself. In HTML, put the buttons in `data-ok-alert-action`; a button with `data-ok-alert-close` closes the alert, with the script loaded.

sections.body: These props set the content and behavior. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body:
- **`ok:alert:close`** (cancelable) fires when the close button is pressed. If you don't call `preventDefault()`, the alert is then hidden.
- **Instance:** `runtime.get(element, "alert")` returns `{ close() }`.
- **React:** `onClose` is called when the close button is pressed. Stop rendering the alert to remove it.

sections.body: The alert itself doesn't take focus. Its buttons are native buttons.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- An alert has `role="alert"`, so screen readers announce it as soon as it appears. For messages that aren't urgent, set `role="status"` so the announcement waits politely.
- The icon is decorative. The close button is named by `closeText` ("Close" by default).
- Don't rely on color alone: the icon and the text should also say what kind of message it is.
- Filled and outlined alerts follow the brand colors; standard alerts meet a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

sections.body: An autocomplete is a text field with a list of suggestions. As people type, the list shows the options whose label contains the text, ignoring case and accents. It follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: focus stays in the field, and the arrow keys move a highlight through the list. It is built from components you already know: a **TextField**, **Chips** for several values, **IconButtons** to clear and open, and a **Popover** for the list.
sections.html:
Fruit
  • Apple
  • Banana
  • Cherry
No options
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Pass `options` as strings, or as `{ value, label }` objects when the value you store differs from what people read, such as country codes. The value is the option's `value`: a string, or `null` when nothing is chosen. In HTML, each option is an `li[role=option]` with `data-ok-value`, and `aria-selected` marks the chosen one.
sections.title: Use options and values

sections.body: The value and the input's text are two states. `value` and `onChange` hold the chosen option. `inputValue` and `onInputChange` hold what people type, for example to load options from a server. When the field loses focus, its text goes back to the chosen option's label.
sections.title: Control the value and the text

sections.body: Set `multiple` to keep several values, shown as chips in the field. Backspace in an empty field removes the last one, and each chip has a remove button. `limitTags` shows a number of chips while the field isn't focused, and "+3" for the rest. With `disableCloseOnSelect` and a `renderOption` that draws a checkbox, the list stays open while people pick. In HTML, a `<template data-ok-autocomplete-tag>` holds the chip for new values.
sections.title: Pick several values

sections.body: Set `freeSolo` when the options are only suggestions: any text is a value, and Enter commits it. A free solo field has no open button. Add `disableClearable` for a search field without the clear button.
sections.title: Accept any text

sections.body: `variant` (`outlined`, `filled`, `standard`), `size` (`medium`, `small`), `label`, `placeholder`, `helperText` and `error` work as on a TextField. `renderOption` draws richer options, such as a code on a **Label** next to each country.

sections.body: Every option works the same way in both versions: a prop in React, an attribute in HTML. Values that aren't listed fall back to the default.
sections.title: Options

sections.body: These props set the options, the value and the texts. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body:
- **`ok:autocomplete:change`** (cancelable) fires with `detail.value`.
- **`ok:autocomplete:open`** and **`ok:autocomplete:close`** fire with `detail.reason`.
- **Instance:** `runtime.get(element, "autocomplete")` returns `{ value, setValue(value), isOpen, open(), close() }`. `setValue` doesn't fire events.
- **React:** `onChange(value)`, `onInputChange(text)` and `onOpenChange(open, reason)`.

sections.body: Focus stays in the field. The highlighted option is announced through `aria-activedescendant`.

sections.body:
- Give the field a `label`: it names the combobox and the list.
- The clear and open buttons are named ("Clear", "Open" / "Close") and out of the tab order: the keys do the same in the field.
- Chips have named remove buttons ("Remove Apple").
- Options are 34px tall. The highlighted and the chosen options have their own background.
- "No options" is shown in the list when nothing matches.

sections.body: An avatar shows a person or an entity: a picture, initials or an icon in a circle. If the picture fails to load, the avatar shows its children, the first letter of `alt`, or a person icon, so it never stays empty.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Without a picture, put initials or an icon inside. Set `color` to tint the background: `default` is grey, the palette colors use white or dark text. Initials scale with the avatar. When the avatar is the only place that names a person, give it `role="img"` and an `aria-label`.

In HTML, write the visible avatars and the surplus avatar with `data-ok-avatar-surplus`. Set `spacing` to `small` for a tighter overlap.

- Initials and icons are decorative by default. Give the avatar `role="img"` and `aria-label` when it's the only place that says who it is.

sections.body: A backdrop dims the whole page and shows its content in front of it, centered. Use it for a loader while your app saves or loads data. The content is white, so a `CircularProgress` with `color` set to `inherit` matches it. In the example, a click anywhere on the backdrop hides it.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Open the backdrop when the work starts and close it when the work ends, whether it succeeds or fails. People can't dismiss a backdrop with the keyboard, so never leave it open after the work is done. In HTML, call `open()` and `close()` on the instance. In React, derive `open` from your loading state.
sections.html: …
sections.title: Show a backdrop while work runs

sections.body: Set `invisible` to make the backdrop transparent. It still covers the page and catches clicks, so a click outside a custom menu or panel can close it without the page behind reacting.
sections.react: <Backdrop open={open} invisible onClick={() => setOpen(false)} />
sections.title: Block clicks without dimming

sections.body: The backdrop fades in over 250 ms and fades out over 200 ms. When people turn on reduced motion in their system settings, it appears and disappears at once. A closed backdrop stays in the page, hidden, so its fade-out can play. Hidden backdrops don't catch clicks and screen readers skip them.
sections.title: Fade in and out

sections.body: A backdrop doesn't take focus. The page behind it stays reachable with the keyboard, and Escape doesn't close it. Use a backdrop for short waits that end on their own. To ask for a decision, or for anything people must dismiss themselves, use a **Dialog**: it moves focus into itself, keeps the page behind it inert and closes with Escape. Dialogs and drawers have their own backdrop with the same color, so you don't add one.
sections.title: Choose between a backdrop and a dialog

sections.body: These props set the content and the state. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup or triggers.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body:
- **`ok:backdrop:beforeopen`** (cancelable) and **`ok:backdrop:open`** fire on the backdrop, with the trigger in `detail.trigger`.
- **`ok:backdrop:beforeclose`** (cancelable) and **`ok:backdrop:close`** carry `detail.reason`: `trigger` or `api`.
- **Instance:** `runtime.get(element, "backdrop")` returns `{ isOpen, open(trigger?), close(reason?) }`.
- **React:** the backdrop reports nothing itself. Set `open` from your own state, and pass `onClick` to close it on a click.
sections.title: Events and methods

sections.body: The backdrop has no keyboard interaction. Focus stays where it was, usually on the button that opened it.

sections.body:
- Give the content its own name, such as `aria-label="Loading"` on a `CircularProgress`, so screen readers announce what is happening.
- Put text on a paper inside the backdrop, not on the backdrop itself. White text directly on the light theme's backdrop has a contrast ratio of about 3:1, below the 4.5:1 that text needs.
- Close the backdrop when the work ends. Keyboard users can't dismiss it themselves.

sections.body: A badge puts a small count, dot or status on the corner of something else: an icon, an avatar or text. Wrap the element in the badge, and the badge sits on its top-right corner. Badges need no JavaScript.

sections.body: Breadcrumbs show where the current page sits in your site and link back to each level above it. They are a `nav` landmark with an ordered list of links: Link components in the parent's color, underlined on hover (`color="inherit"`, `underline="hover"`). The last item is the current page: it isn't a link, and it carries `aria-current="page"`. Separators go between the items and screen readers skip them.

sections.body: Put a decorative `svg` before the text of an item. Icons are 20px and follow the item's color. In React, every child of `Breadcrumbs` becomes an item and the separator goes between them. Pass `separator` to replace the slash with text, an icon or ``. In HTML, write each separator in its own `li` with `aria-hidden="true"`, and use `` for a dot.

Pressing the button shows the whole trail and moves focus to the first item that was hidden. sections.body:
- **`ok:breadcrumbs:expand`** (cancelable) fires on the `nav` before a collapsed trail expands.
- **Instance:** `runtime.get(element, "breadcrumbs")` returns `{ collapsed, expand() }`.
- **React:** the expanded state stays inside `Breadcrumbs`. A new `key` collapses the trail again.
sections.title: Events and methods

sections.body: Breadcrumbs use native links and a native button, so they need no extra keys.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- The `nav` is a landmark. Its default name is "breadcrumb". With several trails on a page, give each one its own `aria-label`.
- Mark the current page with `aria-current="page"` and leave it out of the links.
- Separators are hidden from screen readers. Decorative icons need `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Item text uses the secondary text color and the current page the primary one, both with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
- Links and the expand button show a focus ring for keyboard users. The expand button is at least 24px tall.

sections.body:
A button starts an action, such as saving a form or opening a dialog. When it should take the user to another page instead, render it as a link: it keeps the button's look and gets link behavior.

Use one **contained** button for the main action of a view. Use **outlined**, **soft** or **text** buttons for secondary and less important actions, so the main action stands out.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: The variant sets how much a button stands out. From strongest to lightest: `contained`, `soft`, `outlined` and `text`. The default is `text`.
sections.title: Choose a variant

sections.body: Use `primary` for the main action and the status colors to match the meaning of an action, for example `error` for a destructive one. The default, `inherit`, is a neutral color that suits most secondary actions. Use `black` or `white` on light or dark surfaces, such as images.
sections.title: Pick a color

sections.body: Four sizes are available: `sm` (30px), `md` (36px, the default), `lg` (48px) and `xl` (56px). Use `fullWidth` to make a button fill its container, for example for the main action on a phone.
sections.title: Set the size

sections.body: An icon before or after the label helps people recognize an action. In React, pass it as `startIcon` or `endIcon`. In HTML, wrap it in `data-ok-button-icon`. The icon is decorative: the label stays the button's name.
sections.title: Add an icon

sections.body: Set `loading` while an action runs, such as a form submission. The button shows a spinner, is disabled and tells assistive technology that it's busy. With `loadingPosition`, the spinner replaces the start or end icon instead of covering the label.
sections.title: Show that an action is in progress

sections.body: When a button navigates, render it as a link. In React, pass `href`; in HTML, use an `<a>` element with the same attributes. The URL is passed through untouched.

sections.body: Every option works the same way in both versions: a prop in React, an attribute in HTML. Values that aren't listed fall back to the default.
sections.title: Options

sections.body: These props set the content and behavior. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body: Buttons and links are native elements, so the browser provides the keyboard behavior.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- The label text is the button's name. Icons and the loader are hidden from assistive technology.
- Buttons with only an icon need a name: use an **Icon button** with `aria-label`.
- While loading, the button is disabled and marked busy (`aria-busy="true"`). It leaves the tab order until the action ends, so move focus to the result when it's ready.
- Focus is shown with a 2px outline.
- Every size is at least 24 × 24px, so buttons are easy to hit on touch screens.
- Brand-colored buttons use white text on the main color. Some of these combinations are below a contrast ratio of 4.5:1, so keep labels short. Soft buttons use the accessible `text` tone.
sections.title: Accessibility

sections.body: A button group joins related buttons into one control, such as the range picker of a chart. The buttons keep their own actions; the group only lines them up and shares their style. When the buttons should stay pressed to show a choice, use a **Toggle button** group instead.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: In React, set `variant`, `color`, `size`, `disabled` and `disableElevation` on the group: it passes them to every direct child button, and a prop on a child wins. In HTML, write the same attributes on each button. The default variant is `outlined`.
sections.title: Style every button at once

sections.body: Set `orientation` to `vertical` to stack the buttons, for example on narrow screens, where a horizontal group doesn't wrap. Set `fullWidth` to stretch the group to its container.

sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body: Each button in the group is a native button, so the browser provides the keyboard behavior.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- The group has `role="group"`. Give it an `aria-label` when the buttons need a shared context, such as "Range".
- Each button keeps its own name from its label.
- A focused button is drawn above its neighbors, so its focus outline is never hidden.

sections.body: A card groups content and actions about a single subject, such as an article, a product or a contact. A card is a surface built on Paper: it takes Paper's options, with larger corners and a soft card shadow. Inside it, you combine parts: a header, media, content, actions and an action area. Cards need no JavaScript.
sections.html:
Word of the day

serendipity
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: A card takes every Paper option. Set `variant` to `outlined` for a flat card with a thin outline, which suits cards inside other surfaces. Set `elevation` to a level from 0 to 24 for one of Paper's shadows, or add `raised` for the shadow of level 8, such as for a card that is being dragged. The default level, 1, uses the card shadow. Add `square` to remove the corner radius.
sections.html:
Outlined
Raised
sections.title: Change the surface

sections.body: A card header shows a title and an optional subheader, with an avatar at the start and an action at the end. In React, `CardHeader` wraps the title in a Typography `h6` and the subheader in a Typography `body2` in the secondary text color. Pass `titleProps` or `subheaderProps` to change them, or set `disableTypography` to render your own elements. In HTML, write the same parts.
sections.html:
AL
Ada Lane Product designer

Ada leads the design of the mobile app.
sections.title: Add a header

sections.body: `CardMedia` shows a picture, a video or other media at the edge of the card. With `component` set to `img`, `video`, `picture`, `iframe` or `audio`, the element shows the media itself and fills the card's width. Give it a `height`, and write `alt` on a picture. With another element, such as the default `div`, the picture becomes a decorative cover image that fills the element, so give the element a height in your CSS. To load a picture lazily behind a placeholder, set `component` to the Image component.
sections.html: A picture fills the card's width.
sections.title: Show media

sections.body: `CardActions` lays out buttons in a row, usually at the bottom of the card, with 8px between them. Set `disableSpacing` to remove the space, such as for a row of icon buttons. To make the whole card one action, wrap its media and content in `CardActionArea`: a button, or a link when you set `href`. Keep other actions outside the action area, because a button can't contain another one.
sections.html:
Read the article

The whole card opens the article.
sections.react:
import { Button, Card, CardActionArea, CardActions, CardContent, Typography } from "@owlky/react";

export function ArticleCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardActionArea href="#articles">
        <CardContent>
          <Typography variant="h5" component="div">
            Read the article
          </Typography>
          <Typography variant="body2" color="textSecondary">
            The whole card opens the article.
          </Typography>
        </CardContent>
      </CardActionArea>
      <CardActions>
        <Button size="sm" color="primary">
          Share
        </Button>
      </CardActions>
    </Card>
  );
}
sections.title: Add actions

sections.body: Every option works the same way in both versions: a prop in React, an attribute in HTML. Values that aren't listed fall back to the default. The card takes Paper's options, plus `raised`. `CardActions` has its own option.

sections.body: These props set the content and the elements of each part. They aren't options, because HTML writes them as markup.
sections.title: Content and behavior

sections.body: Cards have no events or methods. Listen to the native events of the buttons and links inside them, such as `click` on a `CardActionArea`.
sections.title: Events and methods

sections.body: A card doesn't take focus. Its action area and the controls inside it keep their native keyboard behavior.
sections.title: Keyboard

sections.body:
- A card is a visual surface. To make it a landmark or an item of a list, use an element with that meaning, such as `article` or `li`.
- An action area is one button or link, so its whole content becomes its accessible name. Keep that content short, or set `aria-label` to a shorter name.
- The action area shows a focus ring and a tint when it has keyboard focus.
- Write `alt` on pictures that carry meaning. Cover images of other elements are decorative.
- Text in the header and content uses the primary and secondary text colors, with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 in the light and dark themes.

sections.body: A carousel shows a set of slides one view at a time. People swipe on touch screens, scroll with a trackpad, drag with a mouse, press the arrow keys, or use the controls: arrows, dots, thumbnails and a progress bar. The slides sit in a native scroll container that snaps to each slide, so the carousel scrolls and snaps even before JavaScript loads. The runtime adds the rest: animated moves, loops, effects, autoplay and the state of the controls.

…
…
…
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: `Carousel` is a labelled `section` that holds every part. `CarouselViewport` is the scroll container and holds the `CarouselSlide`s. Add the controls you need anywhere inside the carousel: `CarouselArrows`, `CarouselDots`, `CarouselProgress`, `CarouselThumbs` with a `CarouselThumb` per slide, and `CarouselPlayButton`. You can use several sets at once, for example arrows on the slides and dots under them. To lay controls over the slides, wrap the viewport and those controls in a `CarouselStage` and give each control a `placement`, such as `bottom-end`.

1/5
…
